title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 3 — 4 Main Ideas
subject: ENG-205

cards.term: New Year weather as Gawain wakes
cards.def: Wild-looking weather pours cold rain, the nithering north needles man's nature, sleet scatters creatures, and a whip-cracking wind drives snow into deepening drifts while Gawain sleeps very little as each cock crow brings his destiny closer.

cards.term: Why Gawain wears the lace at departure
cards.def: Gawain does not leave off the lady's lace girdle, binding it twice about his waist not merely for beauty or gold edges but to save his skin when presenting himself without shield or sword to the fatal swing of the axe.

cards.term: Gawain's thanks to the castle
cards.def: Gawain swears that folk in this castle keep courtesy to the forefront, asks that the lordship's lady be loved all her life, and vows that as long as he lives he shall practice every means to repay their kindness.

cards.term: The guide's warning about the chapel
cards.def: The guide says the place is perilous, a wildman brooding and brutal lives there who loves murdering more than his own life, and to pass through unscathed is impossible because he deals death blows without mercy.

cards.term: The guide's offer to hide the truth
cards.def: The guide urges Gawain to ride another road and be rescued by Christ, swearing by God and all saints that Gawain's secret is safe and not a soul will know that Gawain fled in fear from the fellow described.

cards.term: Gawain's reply to the guide's offer
cards.def: Gawain answers the guide, who has offered to keep silent if Gawain flees, that he would be christened a coward if he failed to find the Green Knight, so he will trek to the chapel and take his chances, for those who strive to serve our Lord, our Lord will save.

cards.term: How Gawain reads the Green Chapel mound
cards.def: Finding only a bald knoll with holes and moss like an old cave, Gawain chunters "Green Church? More like the devil's lair where at the nub of night he dabbles in dark prayers," calling it a soulless spot and haunted house.

cards.term: The honing that greets Gawain
cards.def: From behind a hard rock comes a blood-chilling noise like the scream of a scythe ground on a stone or a waterwheel's whine, and Gawain cries that his arrival is honored with the honing of an axe.

cards.term: The Green Knight's welcome at the chapel
cards.def: The Green Knight vaults the stream with the axe shaft, greets Gawain that his visit keeps his vow, and says Gawain has timed his arrival like a true traveler, honoring the terms that entwine them together.

cards.term: First blow and the flinch shame
cards.def: When Gawain shrinks at the shoulders from the descending axe, the Green Knight swerves and goads that this is not Gawain of good name, for the green man never blinked when his head went flying to his feet.

cards.term: Gawain's vow after the first feint
cards.def: Gawain confesses he flinched at first but will not fail, urging the Green Knight to be brisk with the blow because once his head is unhitched it is off once and for all.

cards.term: Second blow and stone-still courage
cards.def: On the second swing Gawain never moves a muscle but stands stone-still like a tree stump anchored by a hundred roots, so the Green Knight leaves him unscathed and mocks him to pluck up courage.

cards.term: Third blow: nick and blood on snow
cards.def: The third axe hurtles down, skews aside, skims the skin, and finely snicks the fat of the flesh so bright red blood shoots from body to earth onto the snowy ground.

cards.term: Gawain ends the beheading game
cards.def: After the nick Gawain leaps, helmets, shields, and brandishes his sword, saying enough swiping, one axe attack—that's all, now keep the covenant agreed in Arthur's hall.

cards.term: How the three hunts map onto the three blows
cards.def: The Green Knight explains the first feint matched Gawain's truthful return of gains, the second miss matched the kisses returned after Lady Bertilak's kisses, and the third nick matched the day Gawain strayed by keeping the girdle.

cards.term: Bertilak's reveal of the bedroom plot
cards.def: Bertilak says the belt belongs to him, woven by his wife, and that he sent her to test Gawain, so the wooing and kisses were all his work, yet Gawain remains by far the most faultless fellow on earth.

cards.term: Pearl-and-pea praise of Gawain
cards.def: The Green Knight says that as a pearl is more prized than a pea which is white, in good faith so is Gawain amongst gallant knights, even after naming the little fault of the girdle.

cards.term: Why the Green Knight blames Gawain less
cards.def: The Green Knight says Gawain lacked loyalty not because he is wicked or a womanizer but because he loved his own life, so the fault is a little thing and the blame is lighter.

cards.term: Gawain's curse and flinging of the girdle
cards.def: Shocked and ashamed, Gawain curses cowardice and covetousness, grabs the girdle, ungathered its knot, and flings it in fury as his downfall and undoing, confessing treachery and untruth have totally failed him.

cards.term: The Green Knight's absolution
cards.def: The green lord laughs that the harm is wholly healed, that confessing frees Gawain from fault, and that penance at the axe has purged him as polished and pure as the day he was born.

cards.term: Gawain's speech on womanly guile
cards.def: Gawain answers Bertilak by commending the ladies yet listing Adam, Solomon, Samson with Delilah, and David with Bathsheba as men wrecked by women's wiles, asking to be cleared of his crime as they were charmed.

cards.term: Why Gawain will still wear the girdle
cards.def: Gawain tells Bertilak he will wear the gift not for gold or workmanship but as a sign of his sin and a sad reminder that the frailty of his flesh is man's biggest fault whenever pride in prowess swells.

cards.term: Morgan le Fay's plot against Camelot
cards.def: Bertilak reveals that Morgan guided him in green guise to Arthur's hall to put pride on trial, test what distinction and trust the Round Table deserves, and frighten Guinevere with a head-holding specter.

cards.term: Morgan's kinship to Gawain
cards.def: Bertilak says the ancient woman in his home is Gawain's aunt, Arthur's half sister, daughter of the duchess of Tintagel who through Uther was mother to Arthur the king.

cards.term: How Camelot turns the lace into honor
cards.def: Back at court Gawain shows the scar and lace as symbols of sin, but Arthur comforts him and the whole Table laughs in accord that every knight should bear the slanting green belt as their shared sign.
